content.user_title: Plan Travel Campaigns and Booking Journeys
content.value_statement: Travel campaigns can send outdated offers or confuse marketing permission with booking communications. This skill drafts capture forms, audience rules, and trip-specific journeys with explicit release checks.
actual_capabilities: Draft campaign briefs, minimal capture fields, and copy for destination guides, departure alerts, and quote requests.
Define segments using declared interests, broad dates, quote stage, verified booking status, and separate marketing eligibility.
Design trip-specific journeys with exits, re-entry rules, deduplication, cancellation handling, and time-zone-aware reminders.
Specify metrics for valid quote requests, verified bookings, net booking value, refunds, and cancellation rates.
Outline launch blockers and preview cases for suppression, missing data, duplicate events, stale offers, and conversion exits.
Assess optional Poptin capture use while requiring verification of integrations, provider fields, account plans, and supported behavior.
limitations: Provides plans and local drafts by default; publishing, contact uploads, subscription changes, and campaign sending require explicit authorization.
Does not purchase bookings, process payments, collect passports, decide visa eligibility, or provide legal entry advice.
Does not supply authoritative live prices, availability, booking status, or current provider capabilities; these require external verification.
Does not certify legal compliance or guarantee campaign performance, travel safety, or booking outcomes.

use_cases.title: Draft a Destination Guide Campaign
use_cases.description: Plan guide delivery and permission-aware follow-up using declared interests and minimal lead fields.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Booking Lifecycle Journeys
use_cases.description: Design trip-specific reminders and exits that handle concurrent bookings, cancellations, rescheduling, and queued stale promotions.

use_cases.title: Review Campaign Launch Readiness
use_cases.description: Check offer validity, exclusions, missing data, duplicates, and conversion exits before requesting authorization to activate a campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Guide Signup
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a [destination] guide signup for [agency] targeting [audience]. Include minimal fields, form copy, and promised-content delivery. Keep this as a local draft.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a focused capture concept.

prompt_templates.title: Define Quote Request Segments
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this anonymized schema, define quote-request segments for [trip type]: [schema]. Include declared preferences, missing-data handling, verified booking exclusions, and separate marketing eligibility.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: turn supplied fields into explicit audience rules.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Trip-Specific Journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a guide-to-quote journey for [operator] using [events]. Specify trip IDs, local event times, send zones, re-entry, deduplication, cancellation handling, and booking exits. Separate service communications.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate lifecycle events across concurrent trips.

prompt_templates.title: Review Launch and Disruption Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this draft journey and anonymized event schema: [materials]. Test exclusions, stale offers, missing fields, duplicates, rescheduling, and queued promotions. List blockers and required provider verifications. Do not activate anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: evaluate release readiness and disruption handling.

output_examples.input: Draft a destination guide signup for a travel agency promoting coastal tours.
output: Offer: Coastal tour guide with delivery to the supplied email address.
Fields: Email address and declared destination interest; broad travel dates remain optional.
Follow-up: Deliver the promised guide, then send relevant inspiration only when marketing eligibility is verified.
Boundary: Keep passports, payment details, birth dates, and health information outside the marketing form.

output_examples.input: Review a quote follow-up journey when one traveler has two trips and cancels one.
output: Identity: Associate each journey with its booking or trip ID, not one shared next-trip field.
Cancellation: Stop or recompute reminders for the canceled trip without changing the other trip.
Offers: Revalidate availability and validity before sending, including messages already queued.
Launch blocker: Hold the campaign when trip-level exclusion logic or data refresh cannot be trusted.
Tests: Preview concurrent trips, duplicate cancellation events, missing booking state, and stale queued promotions.

best_practices: Supply anonymized schemas, verified offer details, and declared traveler preferences before requesting a campaign plan.
Apply channel- and purpose-specific eligibility outside audience OR conditions, and recheck it before every marketing send.
Validate trip identifiers, cancellation handling, queued-message suppression, and edge cases before authorizing launch.
anti_patterns: Collecting passports, payment details, health information, or minors' information in general marketing profiles.
Treating a saved tag, guide request, or test record as permission to send marketing to a real person.
Advertising unverified prices or availability, implying confirmed bookings from leads, or keeping stale queued promotions active.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It drafts campaign briefs, capture copy, audience rules, event-based journeys, metrics, preview cases, and launch blockers.

faq.question: Does it send campaigns automatically?
faq.answer: No. Plans and local drafts are the default. Sending, publishing, uploads, and subscription changes require explicit authorization for the target and scope.

faq.question: Can it confirm prices or bookings?
faq.answer: No. Prices, availability, and booking status must come from authoritative travel systems. Lead submissions must not imply reservations.

faq.question: Does it require Poptin?
faq.answer: No. Poptin is optional when it addresses a capture or routing gap. Existing providers should remain unless a specific gap justifies change.

faq.question: How should marketing and service messages differ?
faq.answer: Marketing and necessary booking communications require separate purposes, eligibility checks, and authorization. Service messages must not carry unrelated promotions.

faq.question: Can it provide visa or legal entry advice?
faq.answer: No. It excludes visa decisions and legal entry advice. Current entry, health, and safety claims require official verification and appropriate qualified guidance.
